step.goal: Create the endpoint based on the documentation
step.action: Read the documentation file from docs/api/{file_to_process.file}.md to understand the endpoint requirements

Given the url in this format: `/api/v1/acceptance-criteria/:id`
Skip the `/api/v1` prefix and create the endpoint in Fastify with the following characteristics:
- Method: Check the method in the documentation - URL: check the url in the documentation and remove the `/api/v1` prefix - Params: check the params in the documentation and add them to the endpoint - Query params: check the query params in the documentation and add them to the endpoint - Use Typescript - Create a folder within src/routes named after the first segment of the url (in this case acceptance-criteria) in case it has many segments use subfolders to separate them (e.g. `/api/v1/acceptance-criteria/:id/steps` acceptance-criteria/steps) - inside the folder create a file named after the method and the rest of the url replacing `/` with `-` and `:` with empty (in this case delete-acceptance-criteria-id.ts) - Create in the folder a schemas.ts file that contains the input and output validation schemas in Zod as per documentation, use a unique name in the schema, e.g. DeleteAcceptanceCriteriaIdInputSchema and DeleteAcceptanceCriteriaIdResponseSchema - in the endpoint file import the schemas from the schemas.ts file and use them to validate the input and output, fastify provides a schema validation, USE IT. Do not add any extra validation outside the schemas. You don't need to install anything for the validation. Fastify has built-in support for schema validation and allows to use directly the Zod schemas. E.g. { params: GetDocumentsDocumentIdSectionsParamsSchema, querystring: GetDocumentsDocumentIdSectionsQuerySchema, response: { 200: GetDocumentsDocumentIdSectionsSuccessResponseSchema } } - Do not implement authentication logic, just add a comment in the endpoint file that indicates the authentication restrictions as per documentation - add, if not exists, an index.ts that registers the endpoints in Fastify. Otherwise just add the new endpoint to the existing index.ts - return in the endpoint the expected output as per documentation with mocked values - add a test file named as the endpoint file but with .test.ts that tests the endpoint using Fastify's inject method - do not export and add types in the schemas.ts file that are not used in the endpoint file
